_comment: BP1-RAILS execution seam. A LOOKUP TABLE, not a second orchestrator. rails.py::resolve_model(tier) reads tiers.<tier>.model. Two tiers today: mechanical -> the cheapest Claude model string; reasoning -> claude-opus-4-8. The 'engine' field is the swap point: a local engine (harness/rope/exec_ollama.py, already contract-complete) becomes the mechanical tier by changing engine to 'ollama' and pointing model at a local model name - NO change to rails.py, because rails.py only ever looks the value up. Do NOT build the local engine here (Target 4 scope); the seam contract is the deliverable. Design note: harness/battleplan/notes/RAILS_SEAM.md.

mechanical.why: cheapest available Claude model string (Haiku 4.5) - the default for mechanical/low-reasoning legs so trivial work does not spend Opus tokens

reasoning.why: the reasoning tier default named by the mission brief

referee.why: BP2-METER T2: the referee/adjudication tier (Fable 5). A LOOKUP ONLY - orchestrate.ps1 resolves a leg's tier=referee to this model via `rails.py resolve referee`; nothing else decides a model. If the CLI alias cannot be honoured at dispatch (preflight runs/2026-09-01/preflight.json proved claude-fable-5 resolves), the orchestrator falls back to $manifest.model (reasoning) and the ledger row records the fallback.

claude.note: the shipped engine; today's only wired path

ollama.note: NOT built by BP1-RAILS. Documented so a future editor flips a tier's engine to 'ollama' and sets model to a local model name; runner.py::claude_cmd already branches on SYNAPSE_ROPE_ENGINE. Zero rails.py change - that is the point of a lookup seam.
